record.original_question: In the same setting where S={∑_{j=1}^∞ x_j\mid x_j\in K_j} for compact sets K_i\subseteq ℝ with 0\in K_i and \operatorname{diam}(K_i)	o 0, and where R_z={∑_{i=z+1}^∞ x_i\mid x_i\in K_i} denotes the tail set, what conditions on the tails R_z guarantee that S is an interval or a finite union of intervals?

evidence.quote:
2. Under what conditions on the tail Rz will this set be an interval or a finite
union of intervals?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(K_i)_{i\geq 1}$ be a sequence of nonempty compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ with $0 \in K_i$ for every $i$ and with $\operatorname{diam}(K_i) \to 0$ as $i \to \infty$. Define the achievement (subsum) set
$$S = \Bigl\{ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} x_j : x_j \in K_j \text{ for every } j \Bigr\},$$
and for each integer $z \geq 0$ define the tail set
$$R_z = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=z+1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for every } i > z \Bigr\}.$$
Note that $S$ is a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ containing $0$, and that $S = R_0$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the tail sets $R_z$, under which $S$ is a (closed) interval, and conditions under which $S$ is a finite union of (nondegenerate) closed intervals.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on subsums of null sequences. Known classification results (Guthrie–Nymann, Nitecki, Banakh et al.) state that subsum sets of absolutely summable sequences are finite unions of closed intervals, Cantor sets, or Cantorvals, but a clean characterization of the interval / finite-union-of-intervals case in the more general compact-set framework via conditions on the tails $R_z$ does not appear to have been established. No publication resolving this specific question was found.

status_evidence.title: Cantorvals and Subsum Sets of Null Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: The subsum set of an absolutely summable sequence is a finite union of compact intervals, a Cantor set, or a symmetric Cantorval.
status_evidence.claim: Trichotomy for subsum sets is known, but tail-based characterization of the interval case is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions (arXiv:2012.00813)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open questions about achievement sets, including conditions on tails $R_z$ for $S$ to be an interval or finite union of intervals.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as an open question in this survey.
